question.name: Question 1
question.problem: A data set has mean $\overset{―}{x}=17$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=4.06.$ Find the $z$-score of an observation $x=12.3,$ giving your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
The $z$-score of an observation $x$ is defined by

$$
z=\frac{x-\overset{―}{x}}{\sigma }.
$$

The $z$-score represents how many standard deviations an observation is above or below the data set's mean.

Here, we're told that the mean is $\overset{―}{x}=17,$ and we can calculate the standard deviation as

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{4.06}.
$$

So, the $z$-score of the observation $x=12.3$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{x-\overset{―}{x}}{\sigma } \\  & ≈\frac{12.3-17}{\sqrt{4.06}} \\  & ≈-2.33\end{aligned}
$$

to $2$ decimal places.

The z-score of an observation x is defined by

z=x−x―σ.

σ=σ2=4.06.

z=x−x―σ≈12.3−174.06≈−2.33 to 2 decimal places.

EXPLANATION

The z-score of an observation x is defined by

z=x−x―σ.

The z-score represents how many standard deviations an observation is above or below the data set's mean.

Here, we're told that the mean is x―=17, and we can calculate the standard deviation as

σ=σ2=4.06.

So, the z-score of the observation x=12.3 is given by

z=x−x―σ≈12.3−174.06≈−2.33 to 2 decimal places.

solution.reasoning: The standard deviation is \sqrt{4.06}, so z=(12.3-17)/\sqrt{4.06}≈-2.33257, which rounds to -2.33 (option a).
